title: Finite-quotient product comparison and cofinal local ideals
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], S a finite commutative R-algebra [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and p a prime ideal. Set A = R_p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], B = A\otimes_R S [def-weil-module-base-change], J = pB, and Q = {q prime in S : q contracts to p}. For each q in Q let psi_q : B\to S_q be an S-algebra map agreeing on r\otimes 1 with the canonical localized map R_p\to S_q. Write K_q = J S_q for the image ideal along psi_q and M_q for the maximal ideal of S_q. Then K_q is contained in M_q and there exists an integer c >= 1 with M_q^c contained in K_q. For every integer n >= 0, the canonical ring map B/J^n\to\prod_{q\in Q} S_q/K_q^n induced by the psi_q is bijective.

source.place: Tag 07N9, quotient product equality in the proof; Tags 00JA, 00CT and 0394 for its algebraic ingredients

proof.text: Identify B as the localization of S at the images of R minus p. Its maximal ideals above pA correspond to Q and its localizations are S_q. The prescribed values of psi on A and its S-algebra property identify it with the canonical maps on pure tensors, hence everywhere.

For n > 0, A/(pA)^n is Artinian local. The quotient B/J^n is finite over this ring, so its spectrum is finite discrete. The product-of-localizations isomorphism and localization of quotients give precisely the displayed finite-quotient product map. For n = 0 both sides are zero rings; an empty Q is also covered.

S is Noetherian because it is finite over R, and S_q is Noetherian by localization. The special fibre at q is a localization of the finite-dimensional algebra B/(pA)B, hence Artinian local. Its only prime is its maximal ideal. Thus K_q is contained in M_q and its radical equals M_q. Finite generation of M_q and the radical-power lemma give M_q^c contained in K_q; increasing c to c+1 ensures c >= 1.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07N9, finite-level algebraic part preceding passage to the inverse limit

mathlib_searches.query: For a finite algebra over a local Noetherian ring the quotient by a power of the maximal ideal is the product of localized quotients and the extended ideal contains a power of each local maximal ideal
mathlib_searches.results: IsLocalRing.finite_quotient_iff requires a finite residue field; Ideal.finite_quotient_pow concerns cardinal finiteness; DedekindDomain quotient comparison results require a Dedekind domain. No exact statement.
Ideal.comap_map_of_bijective and maximal-ideal transport results assume an already bijective map; they do not prove the localized finite-quotient product comparison.

MaximalSpectrum.toPiLocalizationEquiv is the Artinian product ingredient; Localization.Ideal has the quotient-localization instance; Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg gives cofinal powers. lean/Sheaf and upstream have no combined finite-quotient comparison. FiniteAfterCompletion has the completion comparison but is not a finite-quotient theorem.

mathlib_searches.query: For a finite algebra localized at a prime the quotient by each power of the base ideal is canonically the product of its localized quotients

from.place: algebraic finite-quotient comparison and cofinal ideal bounds, before inverse-limit construction

lean.statement:
theorem completion_localizedAlgebra_finite_quotients
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    let A := Localization.AtPrime p
    let B := A ⊗[R] S
    letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := R) (A := A) (B := S)
    let J := p.map (algebraMap R B)
    let Q := p.primesOver S
    ∀ (ψ : ∀ q : Q, B →ₐ[S] Localization.AtPrime q.1),
      (∀ (q : Q) (r : A), ψ q (r ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : S)) =
        Localization.localRingHom p q.1 (algebraMap R S)
          (Ideal.LiesOver.over (P := q.1) (p := p)) r) →
      let K := fun q : Q ↦ J.map (ψ q).toRingHom
      (∀ q : Q, K q ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1) ∧
        ∃ c : ℕ, 1 ≤ c ∧
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1)) ^ c ≤ K q) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Bijective
        (RingHom.pi (fun q : Q ↦
          Ideal.quotientMap ((K q) ^ n) (ψ q).toRingHom (by
            rw [← Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap, Ideal.map_pow])) :
          (B ⧸ J ^ n) →+* (∀ q : Q, Localization.AtPrime q.1 ⧸ (K q) ^ n))
